incidents.note: No manager was listening on the initially probed default port 8090.
The installed macOS config used port 8099 and contained no image profiles; an isolated benchmark config was created without changing the user config.
Linux workflow weight names were mapped to the installed macOS FP8 variants without changing prompts, cases, steps, dimensions, seeds, or scoring criteria.
Initial isolated instance model IDs omitted the catalog storage-tier prefix; corrected to benchmark-images-comfyui-generation/* before inference.
A diagnostic shell loop used the reserved zsh variable status and stopped after submission; the submitted job was preserved and inspected separately.
The public manager and adapter normalized ComfyUI validation details to generic HTTP 400; the isolated diagnostic adapter was extended to persist the validation body inside the macOS results area.

Qwen and FLUX workflows were rejected by ComfyUI validation in 2-4 ms because auxiliary CLIP/VAE filenames required installed subdirectory-qualified names. All ten non-executed attempts were removed from model totals and queued for rerun.

On macOS, unloading the AI-Lab ComfyUI adapter left its child ComfyUI process alive; subsequent adapters reused it. Benchmark profiles remain serial, but process-lifecycle cleanup requires a separate core fix outside the permitted image/macOS write scope.

Qwen composition entered model execution but the manager terminated the request at the default 120-second first-byte timeout. It is excluded from model success/failure totals; the isolated image-generation timeout was raised to 1800 seconds and the case was queued for rerun.
The following Qwen typography attempt was cancelled through the public API while the common timeout was being corrected; it is excluded from model totals and queued for rerun.

FLUX UNET validation required the installed subdirectory-qualified filename flux2_dev_fp8mixed/flux2_dev_fp8mixed.safetensors. Five 2-5 ms rejected attempts were excluded from model totals and queued for rerun.

FLUX reached SamplerCustomAdvanced but failed during FP8 dequantization with RuntimeError: Undefined type Float8_e4m3fn. This is runtime/model-format incompatibility, not OOM or a semantic model failure.
The installed ComfyUI Python runtime reports torch 2.13.0 with MPS unavailable; generation ran on CPU fallback. The global runtime was not modified because writes were restricted to image/macOS.
Two dedicated FLUX diagnostic prompts were executed only to recover the masked runtime exception; they are excluded from fixture totals.
